oracle_provenance: Direct arithmetic from the standard ppm (parts-per-million frequency error) definition, error_hz/nominal_hz*1e6; hand-verified independently before implementation (48000 Hz at 100 ppm relative error -> 4.8 samples/s drift), not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded digital-audio clock-drift accumulation and buffer-margin check between two clock domains from declared ppm frequency errors; not measured real-hardware clock behavior or continuous-ASRC verification.

cases.question: Over a short resync interval, does the accumulated sample drift stay comfortably within the buffer's half-full margin?
When the resync interval is stretched well past the time needed to exhaust the half-buffer margin, is that flagged rather than silently accepted?
At exactly the predicted time-to-exhaust-half-buffer, does accumulated drift equal the half-buffer size (the model's own self-consistency check)?
Must a non-positive or fractional buffer size be rejected rather than silently used?

When both clock domains share the identical ppm error (a plausible confound: are they actually independent, or secretly synchronized?), does the model correctly predict zero relative drift regardless of how long the resync interval runs?
